title: Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening
author: Robert Frost
text:
Whose woods these are I think I know.
His house is in the village though;
He will not see me stopping here
To watch his woods fill up with snow.
My little horse must think it queer
To stop without a farmhouse near
Between the woods and frozen lake
The darkest evening of the year.
He gives his harness bells a shake
To ask if there is some mistake.
The only other sound’s the sweep
Of easy wind and downy flake.
The woods are lovely, dark and deep,
But I have promises to keep,
And miles to go before I sleep,
And miles to go before I sleep.

lines.text: Whose woods these are I think I know.
lines.prior_rhetoric: Inversion + hedge: ownership comes first; “I think” qualifies certainty. Whose / His also share /h…z/ across the line openings.
lines.grammar: Sentence closes; the fronted clause ends after “are”.
lines.delivery: Flow, or pause after are ‖ before the statement of knowledge.

lines.text: His house is in the village though;
lines.prior_rhetoric: Alliteration: His / house share /h/. The owner is associated with the village. Whose / His: pararhyme; E5 · E7 · E9 · E10.
lines.grammar: Main clause closes; the sentence continues through line 4.
lines.delivery: A small reset; “though” may sound like an afterthought.

lines.text: He will not see me stopping here
lines.prior_rhetoric: Internal rhyme: He / see / me share EE. will / fill links lines 3–4.
lines.grammar: Line 4 adds the purpose of stopping →
lines.delivery: Carry into To watch, or briefly suspend after here.

lines.text: To watch his woods fill up with snow.
lines.prior_rhetoric: Alliteration: watch / woods, /w/. Snow filling the woods supplies visual imagery.
lines.delivery: Close the thought; stanza silence has no fixed duration.

lines.text: My little horse must think it queer
lines.prior_rhetoric: Anthropomorphism: the speaker attributes “think it queer” to the horse.
lines.grammar: “It” is explained by the following “To stop…” →
lines.delivery: Flow onward, or briefly suspend the horse’s imagined judgment.

lines.text: To stop without a farmhouse near
lines.prior_rhetoric: Contrast develops: an expected farmhouse is absent from this stopping place.
lines.grammar: The stopping gains circumstances; location follows →
lines.delivery: Flow into Between, or lightly separate the added setting.

lines.text: Between the woods and frozen lake
lines.prior_rhetoric: Spatial and visual imagery: woods / frozen lake place the speaker between landmarks.
lines.grammar: The place phrase ends; the time phrase follows →
lines.delivery: Possible caesura after woods ‖; a small reset before line 8.

lines.text: The darkest evening of the year.
lines.prior_rhetoric: Superlative: “darkest” intensifies the setting; it does not by itself establish hyperbole.
lines.grammar: Time phrase and the four-line sentence close.
lines.delivery: Close or linger on year. Do not add a syllable to evening.

lines.text: He gives his harness bells a shake
lines.prior_rhetoric: Auditory imagery: harness bells interrupt the scene. he / his / harness echo /h/.
lines.grammar: Main-clause core; the attributed purpose follows →
lines.delivery: Flow into To ask, or briefly let the bell action register.

lines.text: To ask if there is some mistake.
lines.prior_rhetoric: Personification: “To ask” turns the bell shake into a practical objection.
lines.grammar: The purpose and indirect question close the sentence.
lines.delivery: A completed thought; no direct question mark is printed.

lines.text: The only other sound’s the sweep
lines.prior_rhetoric: Alliteration + sibilance: sound’s / sweep repeat /s/; /z/ adds a voiced hiss.
lines.punctuation: apostrophe in sound’s; no end mark
lines.delivery: Carry sweep into Of; a suspension must preserve their link.

lines.text: Of easy wind and downy flake.
lines.prior_rhetoric: Metaphorical, tactile imagery: “downy” likens the flake’s softness to down feathers.
lines.delivery: A gentle or distinct close; whispering is a reader’s choice.

lines.text: The woods are lovely, dark and deep,
lines.prior_rhetoric: Three-part description: lovely, dark, deep; dark / deep alliterate on /d/.
lines.grammar: Description ends; But introduces a counterstatement →
lines.delivery: lovely ‖ dark is optional; the endpoint pause may be light or strong.

lines.text: But I have promises to keep,
lines.prior_rhetoric: Turn / antithesis at But. Parallel noun + infinitive: promises to keep / miles to go.
lines.grammar: “I have” also governs the following “miles…” phrases →
lines.delivery: Light pause, or continue to let obligations accumulate.

lines.text: And miles to go before I sleep,
lines.prior_rhetoric: Anaphoric opening + repeated ending begin the final pair. go recalls rhyme family A.
lines.grammar: The miles-phrase ends and is immediately repeated →
lines.delivery: Optional pause after go ‖; a short or long gap before line 16.

lines.text: And miles to go before I sleep.
lines.prior_rhetoric: Immediate full-line repetition (epizeuxis); identical sleep / sleep inside monorhyme.
lines.grammar: Repeated phrase and the entire sentence close.
lines.delivery: Firm fall, fading weariness or reflective slowing; none is compulsory.

rhymeOverlap: Perfect / full rhyme matches the last stressed vowel and every sound after it. End / internal locate the match. Masculine classifies the stressed ending. Monorhyme describes a stanza using one rhyme family.

“Masculine” means the rhyme ends on a stressed syllable: mis-TAKE qualifies even though the word has two syllables. In D, different words rhyme perfectly; sleep / sleep is the more specific identical-word case. One repeated pair also belongs to a masculine, end-rhymed, monorhymed stanza.

Smaller echoes: His / is can share IZ in full speech; house returns inside farmhouse. only / easy / downy / lovely share a weak final EE, a vowel echo rather than a full rhyme. These interior echoes do not change the end-rhyme scheme. know / though / snow rhyme by sound despite unlike spellings.
boundaries: The six sentences span lines 1 | 2–4 | 5–8 | 9–10 | 11–12 | 13–16. A semicolon ends a clause in line 2; a comma ends the main clause in line 13. Neither ends its sentence in this supplied text.

Enjambment: syntax continues through unpunctuated ends at 3, 5, 6, 7, 9 and 11. The tightest noun–modifier link is “sweep / Of…”. Some other line ends already complete a smaller unit, even while the sentence continues.

Caesura: an audible pause within a line. After are (1), woods (7), lovely (13) or go (15–16), a reader can pause or flow. Only lovely has a printed comma at that internal position. Lengthening or a pitch change can mark a boundary without silence.

Dotted feet in 8 and 14 separate the expected beat from light speech. EEV-ning has two syllables; PRAH-mi-siz has three. A metrical position, word stress and emotional emphasis are related but distinct.
rhetoric: Observation and ownership (1–4) → imagined practical objection (5–10) → renewed sensory attention (11–13) → obligation and self-address (14–16). “But” is the explicit turn. Repeated woods links the opening, middle and final assessment.

Sound devices overlap too: sound’s / sweep is both alliteration and sibilance; the EE of see, sweep, easy, deep, keep and sleep supplies assonance across the poem. Whose begins with /h/, so Whose woods is not /w/ alliteration.

The last two lines are one repeated event viewed several ways: full-line repetition / epizeuxis; anaphoric beginning; repeated ending; identical end rhyme. A second delivery can renew resolve, expose weariness, or make the statement newly reflective.

Interpretive alternatives: literal travel before sleep; duties before rest; a larger life-journey or mortality association. These readings may coexist. The words do not establish “sleep = death” or prove that the two sleeps change meaning. The poem does not narrate a departure.
attribution: Wording and punctuation follow the supplied poem, including deep, in line 13. Stress alternatives, grammar labels and device-to-effect connections are close readings offered here; they are not attributed to a recording by Frost. Device labels describe evidence; suggested effects and symbolic readings remain interpretations.
